svg.title: CloudMart identity and access diagram
svg.desc: How CloudMart authenticates and authorises. Microsoft Entra ID issues user tokens through the SPA and API app registrations (scope access_as_user, app role CloudMart.Admin), service tokens for the Payments and Shipping app roles, and federated tokens for AKS workload identity and the pipeline's service connection. A matrix lists every Azure RBAC role, Cosmos DB data-plane role, Azure SQL and PostgreSQL database role, Redis access policy and Entra app role held by each identity, including the phase 14 data lake's and the phase 15 legacy server's. No keys or connection-string secrets are used, with one exception: phase 13's VPN pre-shared key, a @secure() parameter that defaults to a new GUID on each deployment, kept only on the two VPN connections.
svg.text: Who signs in, how services get tokens, and every role each identity holds. Every arrow is an Entra ID token: no keys or connection-string secrets anywhere, with one exception.
The exception is phase 13's VPN pre-shared key, a @secure() parameter that defaults to a new GUID on each deployment, kept only on the two VPN connections.

svg.text: ¹ Phase 16 moves the payment-gateway key: only the Payments identity can read it, and the API and Functions lose access.
² Cosmos DB data-plane RBAC (sqlRoleAssignments: Built-in Data Contributor). It is not Azure RBAC, so the IAM blade doesn't show it.

³ Database roles, not Azure RBAC. Azure SQL: contained users (CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER) from deploy/sql/grant-managed-identities.sql, including the Data Factory's read-only user; ddladmin only because the apps create their schema.

PostgreSQL (phase 4's alternative engine, phase 15's target): deploy/postgres/grant-managed-identities.sql gives the API identity USAGE and CREATE on schema public, so it owns the tables it creates, and the Functions identity read and write on them.
⁴ Entra app roles (application permissions) on the services' app registrations, assigned through Microsoft Graph, not Azure RBAC. The phase 11 Event Hubs secondary gets the same roles as the primary.
Control plane is not data plane

text.tspan: Owner and Contributor manage resources, but read
no blobs, secrets or messages: that takes a data role.

svg.text: No keys on the data services

text.tspan: Shared keys off on Storage; local auth off on Service
Bus and Event Hubs; Cosmos DB keys off; SQL Entra-only.
Sender or receiver, never both; a secret readable by one
service; a database per service; app roles per API.
